issues.issue: Whether s. 22 of the Regulations shields the applicant from a s. 16(1) misrepresentation finding
issues.applicant_position: Section 22 policy should forgive s. 16(1) breaches and refugees may lie to escape persecution.
issues.respondent_position: Act provisions are clear; Lhamo, a family reunification case, supports the refusal.
issues.result_text: Section 22 relieves claimants only from s. 40(1), not s. 16(1); policy cannot override clear statutory terms.

issues.issue: Whether the visa officer was obliged to proceed under s. 40(1) or the refugee claim process instead of s. 16(1)
issues.applicant_position: Visa officer could have avoided s. 16(1) and applied s. 40(1) principles.
issues.respondent_position: Minister concedes the officer could have used the refugee claim procedure and discretion to avoid s. 16(1).
issues.result_text: No obligation to avoid s. 16(1) and no unreasonableness in applying it.

issues.issue: Whether the refusal reasonably addressed the applicant's procedural fairness response
issues.applicant_position: Refusal should have acknowledged her procedural fairness response and reasons for untruthfulness.
issues.result_text: Omitting the acknowledgment from the refusal, though preferable, does not make the decision unreasonable.

issues.issue: Whether s. 40(1)(a) materiality requirements apply to the refusal
issues.applicant_position: Any misrepresentation concerned identity and was not material to the fear of persecution assessment.
issues.result_text: Visa officer did not intend to apply s. 40(1)(a), so the materiality concept does not apply.
